newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close sharply higher.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed sharply higher as speculators and investors flocked to the bourse in the absence of trading on most of the other stock exchanges, brokers said on Monday.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 26.08 points or 3.86 percent, higher at 702.15.
"Although the sentiment seems to be bullish the future trend of the market would become clear only after other stock exchanges reopen," said Manoj Aggarwal of brokers Multiple Investments.
Traders said recovery was also fuelled by last week's central bank announcement that it will cut banks' cash reserve ratio to 10 percent with two 0.5 percentage point cuts in January.
Some brokers said the rise in share prices was in line with the general trend of buying on the first day of the settlement period.

"The sentiment is upbeat as the market is expecting the Prime Minister to announce some measures to encourage the stock markets in his meeting with the industrialists tomorrow," said another broker who asked not to be named.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda is scheduled to meet country's leading industrialists and economists on Tuesday to discuss ways to boost economy.
Reliance Industries rose 7.05 rupees to 210.55 on heavy buying by domestic financial institutions, brokers said.
State Bank of India quoted 9.70 rupees higher at 238.50 and Oriental Bank of Commerce gained 5.55 rupees to 82.90.
TELCO surged 22.40 rupees to 353.95 on speculative buying, brokers said.
